academic_translation:
The bodhisattva who practises the wisdom of the Victors
Knows these aggregates to be empty and unborn from the beginning.
While not in meditative equipoise, they engage in compassion for the realm of sentient beings,
And even in the meantime, they do not decline from the qualities of a Buddha.
translation: The awakening hero practices the wisdom of the Victorious Ones. They know these heaps are empty and never born from the start. When they are not resting in deep thought, they show compassion for the realm of living beings. Even then, they do not lose a Buddha's qualities.

academic_translation:
For example, a skilled person endowed with all qualities,
Who is powerful, invincible, diligent, and knows the methods of the arts,
Who has mastered archery and many fields of craft,
And who knows how to conjure illusions and greatly desires the welfare of beings—
translation: Imagine a skilled person who has every good quality. They are strong, unbeatable, hard-working, and know many arts. They are experts at archery and crafts. They know how to make an illusion and deeply want the good of beings.

academic_translation:
Having fully gathered his father, mother, and wife,
He sets out upon a wilderness path where many enemies dwell;
And emanating many brave and courageous men,
He travels safely and returns home once again—just as,
translation: This person takes his father, mother, and wife on a journey. They walk on a wild path full of enemies. The skilled person magically makes many brave men to protect them. They travel safely and return home again. It is just like that.

academic_translation:
Likewise, at that time, the skilled bodhisattva also
Generates great compassion for all realms of sentient beings,
And having utterly passed beyond the four Māras and the two levels,
Abides in the supreme samādhi and does not touch awakening.
translation: In the same way, the clever awakening hero grows great compassion for the whole realm of living beings. They completely pass beyond the four Maras and the two lower levels. They stay in the highest deep calm. Yet, they do not touch awakening.

academic_translation:
Wind is supported on space, and on that is supported the mass of water;
On that is supported this great earth, and on that are supported beings.
Such is the cause for sentient beings engaging in their karma.
Reflect on this meaning: upon what does space abide?
translation: Wind rests on space. A mass of water rests on the wind. This great earth rests on the water. All beings rest on the earth. This is the cause for living beings doing their deeds. Think about this meaning: what does space rest on?

academic_translation:
Likewise, the bodhisattva who abides in emptiness,
Supported by aspirations that know sentient beings among beings,
Demonstrates many various kinds of activities,
Does not touch nirvāṇa, and does not abide in emptiness.
translation: In the same way, the awakening hero rests in emptiness. They are held up by a wish that understands living beings among all beings. They show many different actions. They do not touch peace beyond sorrow. They also do not just stay in emptiness.

academic_translation:
Whenever a skilled and brilliant bodhisattva
Practices this supreme samādhi of peaceful emptiness,
During that time they do not cultivate signs;
Dwelling in signlessness, they practice peace, utter peace.
translation: A skilled and bright awakening hero practices this highest deep calm of peaceful emptiness. At that time, they do not build up signs. Resting without signs, they practice pure and perfect peace.

academic_translation:
For a bird flying in the sky, there is no place to abide;
It does not abide there, nor does it fall to the ground.
Likewise, a bodhisattva who practices in the doors of liberation
Does not touch nirvāṇa, nor do they engage with signs.
translation: Think of a bird flying in the sky. It has no place to rest up there, but it does not fall to the ground. An awakening hero practicing the doors to freedom is just like that bird. They do not touch peace beyond sorrow, and they do not grasp at signs.

academic_translation:
For example, a man trained in archery shoots an arrow into the sky,
And by continuously following it with other arrows in succession,
He leaves no opportunity for the previous arrow to fall to the ground;
Should that person wish it, that arrow will fall to the ground.
translation: Think of a trained archer shooting an arrow into the sky. He shoots more arrows right behind it in a fast line. His new arrows keep the first one from falling to the ground. That first arrow will only fall when the archer wants it to.

academic_translation:
Likewise, those who practice the supreme perfection of wisdom,
Acting through wisdom, skillful means, strength, and miraculous powers,
As long as their roots of virtue are not complete,
For that long, they do not attain that supreme emptiness.
translation: In the same way, someone might practice the highest perfect wisdom. They act using wisdom, clever ways, strength, and magic powers. They will not reach that highest emptiness until their roots of goodness are fully complete.

academic_translation:
For example, a monk endowed with the supreme power of miracles
Abides in the sky and simultaneously emanates a miraculous display,
Demonstrating walking, pacing, lying down, and sitting;
He feels no weariness, and he has no fatigue.
translation: Think of a monk who has the highest power of magic. He stays up in the sky and shows a wonder all at once. He appears to be walking, pacing, lying down, and sitting. He never gets tired, and he feels no weariness.

academic_translation:
Likewise, a skilled bodhisattva dwelling in emptiness,
Having perfected primordial wisdom and miraculous powers, abides nowhere;
They display an infinite variety of activities to beings,
And for ten million eons, they feel no weariness and have no fatigue.
translation: In the same way, a skilled awakening hero rests in emptiness. They have perfected deep knowing and magic powers, but they do not stay anywhere. They show an endless number of actions to beings. Even after ten million ages, they never get tired or weary.

academic_translation:
For example, just as someone standing at a great precipice
Holds two parasols in both hands and leaps into the sky,
Casting their body into the great abyss,
They do not fall, but travel for as far as it may be.
translation: Imagine someone standing at the edge of a high cliff. They hold two umbrellas in their hands and jump into the sky. They dive into the deep space below, but they do not fall. Instead, they glide through the air for a long way.

academic_translation:
Likewise, the wise bodhisattva, abiding in compassion,
Fully holds the two parasols of skillful means and wisdom;
Contemplating phenomena as empty, as signlessness, and as wishless,
They do not touch nirvāṇa, yet they see phenomena.
translation: In the same way, the wise awakening hero rests in compassion. They hold the two umbrellas of clever ways and wisdom. They see that things are empty, being without signs, and without wishes. They do not touch peace beyond sorrow, yet they still see things.

academic_translation:
For example, just as someone desiring jewels goes to a jewel island,
And, having found jewels, returns home again,
That merchant does not live happily all alone
While leaving their host of family and friends unhappy.
translation: Imagine a person who wants jewels. They travel to a jewel island and bring the treasures back home. That merchant does not enjoy the happiness all alone while leaving their family and friends sad.

academic_translation:
Likewise, the bodhisattva who has gone to the jewel island of emptiness
And attained meditative concentration, faculties, and powers,
Does not delight merely in touching nirvāṇa alone
While leaving sentient beings in suffering.
translation: In the same way, an awakening hero goes to the jewel island of emptiness. There they gain deep focus, abilities, and powers. They do not just enjoy touching peace beyond sorrow by themselves. They do not leave other living beings behind in suffering.

academic_translation:
For example, a merchant seeking profit, in order to know the route,
Goes to whatever intervening cities, towns, and villages there are;
He does not dwell there, nor does he dwell on the jewel island,
And the wise one does not dwell at home, but becomes skilled in the path.
translation: Think of a merchant who travels to learn the route. They visit every city, town, and village along the way. They do not stay there, and they do not stay on the jewel island. This wise person does not stay at home either, but becomes skilled in the path.

academic_translation:
Likewise, the brilliant bodhisattva is skilled in all
The knowledge and liberation of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
They do not dwell in them, nor do they dwell in the primordial wisdom of a Buddha,
And they do not dwell in the unconditioned, but know the ways of the path.
translation: In the same way, a brilliant awakening hero is skilled in the knowledge and freedom of a listener and a solitary Buddha. But they do not stay there, and they do not stay in a Buddha's deep knowing. They do not stay in what is not made by causes, but they understand the ways of the path.

academic_translation:
Whenever, having connected with beings through loving-kindness,
They practice the samādhis of emptiness, signlessness, and the wishless,
Could it be designated that they will attain nirvāṇa,
Or that they are conditioned? That is impossible.
translation: These heroes connect with beings through loving-kindness. They practice the deep calm of emptiness, being without signs, and without wishes. Could anyone say they will just reach a peace beyond sorrow? Or that they are made by causes? That is impossible.

academic_translation:
For example, just as an emanated human body is not invisible,
And can even be designated by a name,
Likewise, a bodhisattva who practices the doors of liberation
Can even be designated by a name.
translation: Think of a magically created human body. It is not invisible, and you can still call it by a name. In the same way, an awakening hero practices the doors to freedom. And they can still be called by a name.

academic_translation:
If, when thoroughly questioned about their conduct and faculties,
A bodhisattva does not fully teach the Dharma of emptiness and signlessness,
And does not explain the Dharma of the irreversible stage,
They should be known as unprophesied.
translation: Someone might ask an awakening hero about their behavior and ability. What if the hero does not fully share the teaching of emptiness and being without signs? What if they do not explain the teaching of the level of never turning back? Then you should know they are not predicted.

academic_translation:
Chapter Five shows the complete realization of the peak:
The stage of an arhat, the primordial wisdom of a pratyekabuddha,
And the three realms, they do not desire even in a dream;
Seeing the Buddhas teaching the Dharma to beings,
This should be known as the prophecy of irreversibility.
translation: Chapter Five shows the full understanding of the peak. These heroes do not want the level of a worthy one, the deep knowing of a solitary Buddha, or the three realms. They do not want them even in a dream! Instead, they see the Buddhas sharing the teaching with beings. You should know this is a prediction of never turning back.

academic_translation:
Seeing in a dream sentient beings dwelling in the three lower realms,
In that instant they make an aspiration to cut the continuum of the lower realms,
And they pacify a mass of fire through the blessing of truth;
This should be known as the prophecy of irreversibility.
translation: In a dream, they might see living beings stuck in the three lower realms. Right in that moment, they make a wish to put an end to the lower realms. They put out a huge fire through the blessing of truth. You should know this is a prediction of never turning back.

academic_translation:
The many harmful spirits and diseases in the human world
Are pacified through the blessing of truth by those endowed with benefit and compassion;
Yet they remain without conceit and do not give rise to pride—
They should be understood as having the prophecy of irreversibility.
translation: There are many harmful spirits and sicknesses in the human world. A person with compassion can calm them through the blessing of truth. Even so, they feel no self-importance and do not show pride. You should know they have a prediction of never turning back.

academic_translation:
However, if those various blessings of truth
Are accomplished, and conceit arises thinking, "I have a prophecy,"
Or if they become conceited at being prophesied by other bodhisattvas,
Those abiding in conceit should be known as having small intelligence.
translation: But maybe someone performs a blessing of truth and feels self-importance. They might proudly think, 'I have a prediction!' Or they might feel self-importance when other awakening heroes give them a prediction. Anyone who holds onto this self-importance has little understanding.

academic_translation:
When Māra approaches on the basis of names,
He speaks thus: "These are the names of you and your parents,
And of your lineage back to the seventh generation of ancestors;
And when you become a Buddha, this will be your name."
translation: Mara might approach you and use names to trick you. He will say, 'These are the names of you and your parents. These are the names of your ancestors for seven generations. When you become a Buddha, this will be your name.'

academic_translation:
"Whatever ascetic practices and yoga you will come to possess,
He declares, 'Your former qualities and conduct were also like this.'
Any bodhisattva who hears such words and becomes conceited
Should be known as fully incited by Māra and having small intelligence.
translation: Mara will tell you about your strict practices and your training. He will say, 'You had these same good qualities in the past.' An awakening hero might hear this and feel self-importance. If they do, they are being pushed by Mara and have little understanding.

academic_translation:
Though they thoroughly rely upon very isolated villages, cities, and mountain valleys,
And upon forests, isolated places, and woodland retreats,
A bodhisattva who praises themselves and deprecates others
Should be known as fully incited by Māra and having small intelligence.
translation: Someone might live far away in quiet villages, cities, and mountain valleys. They might stay deep in the forest or in hidden retreats. Even so, an awakening hero might praise themselves and put down others. You should know that such a person is pushed by Mara and has little understanding.
